subject: Evidence request: sample erase logs + retention policy artifacts
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@clearshore.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: sample erase logs + retention policy artifacts

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SOC 2 readiness audit we need a small package of artifacts showing how Redwood handles tenant data deletions and TTL-based retention. Our auditors asked for: 

- A sample (redacted) tenant erase log covering a single deletion event, including timestamps and job IDs.
- The retention policy doc that describes TTLs and exceptions.
- The runbook or playbook used when a customer requests a tenant erasure.
- Any S3/bucket lifecycle configuration or equivalent that enforces automated archival/deletion.

We don't need full production logs — a single representative trace is fine, but it must show the end-to-end steps your system takes (request received -> orchestration -> storage purge -> audit trail).

Can you supply these artifacts or point me at the shared location? We aim to close this by next Friday (8/6).

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Senior Compliance Manager | ClearShore Financial

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@clearshore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: sample erase logs + retention policy artifacts

Elena — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a redacted evidence pack that contains exactly the pieces you listed. Quick notes: 

- I'll attach a sanitized erase log for a tenant deletion run (job IDs, timestamps, but tenant identifiers redacted).
- Attached is our current retention-policy-v3.pdf (public-facing + internal notes removed).
- I will also include the operational runbook excerpt that describes orchestration and verification steps; it's been sanitized for PII and customer names.
- We'll include the S3 lifecycle configuration JSON that governs archival -> delete after TTL.

Timeline: I'll assemble a package and share a Drive link by EOD Friday (8/2 PT). If auditors need a different format (CSV vs PDF), tell me and I'll adapt.

Attachments included in this email: redwood-tenant-erase-log-20260601.csv (sanitized), retention-policy-v3.pdf

Next steps: If your auditors want a brief walkthrough (15–20 min) of the artifacts, Marissa (CC'd, Customer Success) can join to cover the customer-facing controls.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: sample erase logs + retention policy artifacts

Connor — reviewed the two artifacts and added a small redaction checklist. A few technical clarifications for the auditors that should be in the manifest: 

- The erase job is kicked off by the tenant lifecycle API (auth protected) and stored as an entry in the tenant-operations queue (we'll include the job ID mapping).
- KV-cache invalidation and model-context purge happen before storage deletion; include the timestamped cache flush step.
- For S3, lifecycle rule uses object-tagging "tenant:deleted=true" and expiration-days=30 in our test artifact; prod uses 0-day retention after confirmation window. 

I also recommend we include a short attestation statement (one paragraph) from Security that the redactions preserve auditability while protecting other tenants. Vivek, can you provide that?

I attached a sanitized runbook excerpt (erase-runbook-sanitized.txt) and a sample s3-lifecycle-config.json.

Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@clearshore.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: sample erase logs + retention policy artifacts

Elena — quick customer note: when we run a tenant erase for production customers we follow a 3-step confirmation flow (request -> ops verify -> scheduled purge). For enterprise customers who signed a retention override, we keep a separate attestation in the contract folder; we can provide a redacted pointer if auditors need to see the contractual exception handling.

If ClearShore wants a live 20-min demo of the erase flow, I can book time for Wed 8/4 or Thu 8/5 (US hours).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@clearshore.com>, ClearShore Compliance Team <compliance@clearshore.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 14:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Deliverable: sanitized erase evidence package + manifest (Drive link)

Elena — delivering the sanitized evidence pack per your request. Drive bundle: https://drive.redwood.example.com/Shared/clearshore/evidence-2026-07

Package contents (sanitized):
- redwood-tenant-erase-log-20260601.csv (contains job_id, event_timestamp_utc, step, outcome, operator_id=redacted)
- retention-policy-v3.pdf (public policy + internal appendix removed)
- erase-runbook-sanitized.txt (playbook excerpt showing orchestration, verification, and post-delete verification hooks)
- s3-lifecycle-config.json (example rule used in infra for object expiration and legal_hold handling)
- evidence-manifest-connor-20260729.csv (short mapping: artifact -> explanation -> redaction notes)

Follow-ups: Vivek provided the attestation and it's included in the Drive as "security-attestation-erase-20260729.txt". Marissa can run a 20-min demo if you want; we have availability Wed 8/4 10:00 PT and Thu 8/5 14:00 ET.

Let me know if the auditors need additional metadata (e.g., cryptographic hashes for the sample files, or more granular timestamps).

Best regards,
Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
